extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents/attorneys, and IPOPHL examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules governing prosecution of patent applications before the IPOPHL, including divisionals, publication, search, substantive examination, amendments, appeals, and third-party observations. Targets requirements and procedures applicants and examiners must follow during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration for Requirement of Division
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant disagrees with the requirement of division, a request for reconsideration and withdrawal or modification of the requirement may be filed, giving the reasons therefore. In requesting reconsideration, the applicant must indicate a provisional election of one invention for prosecution, which invention shall be the one elected in the event the requirement becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement will be reconsidered on such request; if repeated and made final, Examiner acts on claims of the elected invention. If final and applicant failed to indicate a provisional election, the first group of claims indicated in the office action will be considered for prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from Requirement for Division
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final requirement for division, the applicant may appeal from the requirement together with full payment of the prescribed fee, subject to rules on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution on elected claims may continue during the appeal; final action/allowance of elected claims deferred until appeal resolved. Appeal may not be allowed if reconsideration was not requested. Applicant may request that the 4‑month period to file a divisional begin only after appeal resolution, subject to fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent Presentation of Claims for Different Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If after an official action the applicant presents claims directed to an invention divisible from the previously claimed invention, such claims, if entered, will be refused and applicant required to limit claims to the invention previously claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments adding claims to a different (divisible) invention will be refused if entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on an application with a generic claim and separate species claims, the Examiner after a complete search on the generic claim shall require the applicant to elect a species to which the claim shall be restricted if no generic claim is finally allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims directed neither to the species nor the genus may not be accepted. Markush-type claims enumerating alternatives as species may be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Divisional Applications — Filing and Content
rubrics_metrics.description: A mandatory divisional application arises from a restriction following lack of unity; a divisional may be examined like the parent and has the benefit of the parent's priority if filed within four months from the date the requirement for division becomes final or after an appeal is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional may give rise to further divisionals; for succeeding mandatory divisionals the 4‑month period is counted from election or when requirement becomes final. Filing must include application form, copy of abstract/description/claims/drawings, proposed amended claims canceling irrelevant claims, a copy of drawings complying with rules, and full filing fee. Divisionals filed beyond 4 months are rejected as invalid, except in specified identical‑application circumstances filed before the earlier application is patented or withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Parent and Divisional Claiming Same Subject-Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent and divisional applications shall not claim the same subject-matter; claims should not be substantially identical in scope or claim subject-matter claimed in the other, even in different words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difference between claimed subject-matter of the two applications must be clearly distinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary Divisional Application Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file a voluntary divisional on a pending application or within four months from date the parent is withdrawn or patented, provided the subject matter does not extend beyond content of the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Succeeding voluntary divisionals may be filed on earlier divisionals under similar timing. Voluntary divisionals accorded same filing date and priority as parent; form requirements same as mandatory divisional. Parent and divisional must not claim same subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of a Divisional Application
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a divisional application, whether earlier, succeeding, mandatory or voluntary, shall be twenty (20) years reckoned from the filing date of the original or first filed parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Concerning Corresponding Foreign Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the Office, applicant shall furnish the date and number of any foreign application relating to the same or essentially the same invention and other documents relating to the foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other documents may include English search reports from major offices, photocopies of cited documents, copies of examination reports/decisions, and other documents facilitating adjudication. Failure to furnish directed documents may result in application being considered withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and Search Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that has complied with formal requirements shall be classified and a search conducted to determine the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office shall use the International Patent Classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the Intellectual Property Search Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Search report drawn up on basis of claims, description and drawings and shall mention documents available that may be considered in assessing novelty and inventive step; distinguish documents by publication date relative to priority and filing; contain classification per IPC; may include documents cited in corresponding foreign searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Application — Standard Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for which a prior art search can be conducted shall be published in the IPOPHL E‑Gazette together with a search document after expiration of 18 months from filing date or priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that cannot be searched (e.g., serious disclosure defects) shall not be published and be deemed forfeited; not published if finally refused/withdrawn/forfeited before technical preparation for publication. Published application will contain bibliographic data, drawings as filed, and abstract. The Office shall notify applicant of publication date and the period within which request for substantive examination must be filed. Director General, with Secretary approval, may prohibit/restrict publication for national security.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT National Phase Listing Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT national phase entry applications shall not be published individually; a list containing bibliographic data of PCT applications entering national phase shall be published after issuance of the National Phase Entry Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Publication of Patent Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may be published before 18 months but not earlier than 6 months from filing if a written request is filed, a waiver on confidentiality under oath attached, the applicant agrees to publication without a search report, and full early publication fees paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Divisional Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional filed within the formality stage of the parent shall be published simultaneously after the 18th month of the parent application. A divisional filed subsequent to publication of the parent shall be published as soon as practicable but accorded a date of publication similar to the parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality Before Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An application not yet published shall not be made available for inspection without applicant's consent. After publication, any interested party may inspect complete description, claims and drawings as filed; marginal notes and exchanges between applicant and Office are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection by other international IP offices pursuant to agreements shall be governed by those agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Review and Notification upon Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon publication, the concerned community shall be notified by the Office (by email or website) in the interest of transparency and improving patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation by Third Parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Within six months from publication any person may present written observations concerning patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability) citing relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations must be a sworn statement with affiant's personal info and circumstances, grounds, payment of fees, substantiated by evidence and may attach prior art. Office will not consider non-complying submissions. Interested parties may request a conference (fees apply); Office acknowledges receipt, may request more info; applicant may comment within 30 days from mailing of communication. Observations, comments, and conference minutes form part of file wrapper and shall be taken into consideration in examination. Third party may be notified of status upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑Party Observations for PCT National Phase
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested party may submit a Third‑Party Observation within six months from date of publication of the PCT national phase entry applications listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Substantive Examination — Timing and Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request for substantive examination together with full payment of corresponding fee shall be filed within six months from date of publication. Substantive examination determines whether application meets patentability requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to request substantive examination and pay fees within prescribed period results in withdrawal of the application. Request is irrevocable and fees not refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Accelerated Substantive Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file a request for accelerated examination with payment of prescribed fee after publication and after the request for substantive examination has been filed, in accordance with accelerated procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval subject to Director of Patents; procedures may be promulgated by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights Conferred by a Published Application
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication the applicant shall have rights of a patentee under Section 76 against any person who, without authorization, exercises rights conferred under Section 71 with respect to the published invention, provided the person had actual knowledge or received written notice identifying the published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action may not be filed until after grant of a patent on the published application and must be within four years from commission of the acts complained of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Prior Art References — Required Data
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing domestic patents provide numbers, dates, patentees and classes. For foreign patents state country, numbers, dates, patentees and other data needed to identify patents; identify particular pages/sheets if only part is involved. For non‑patent publications give author, title, date, relevant pages/plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation Based on Personal Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: If citation of a reference is based on personal knowledge, the data shall be as specific as possible and the reference must be supported, when called for, by an affidavit of the person with personal knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Withdrawal Prior to Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A pending application withdrawn prior to first publication shall not be published and shall be deemed withdrawn. Applicant may improve and file again as a new application, subject to filing fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Inadvertent Publication Despite Voluntary Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant voluntarily withdrew prior to first publication but application was inadvertently published, applicant may file a manifestation informing the Office. The Office shall publish a clarification that the application was inadvertently published and is deemed withdrawn without prejudice to refiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure in such inadvertent publication shall not prejudice novelty; applicant may refile as a new application subject to fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex Parte Prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are prosecuted ex parte by the applicant. The Examiner's role is to ensure only applications complying with law for patentability are granted letters patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest Between Examiner and Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner safeguards public interest by allowing exclusivity only based on valid patent claims covered by the disclosure; applicant or attorney may present arguments to obtain broader protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Actions of the Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: An Examiner's assessment resulting in Official Actions provides the applicant opportunity to improve or clarify claims through amendments; issues resolved become administrative rulings strengthening presumption of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conferences and Interviews with the Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference or interview concerning an Official Action may be requested by applicant/agent/attorney and must be made by filing a written request specifying query, proposed meeting schedules and after payment of required fees. Examiner may decline and reply in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests not in writing will not be entertained. Unscheduled visits or virtual calls will not be entertained. Conferences conducted either in-office during examiner hours (minutes form part of file wrapper) or virtually (recording forms part of file wrapper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Refusal is Not Final
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal by the Examiner based on prior art is preliminary; refusal may involve only claims and not necessarily the invention. Applicant may defend or amend via written response; Examiner's suggestions can help strengthen legal presumption of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of Examiner's Decision to the Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of an Examiner refusing applications are subject to appeal to the Director within a non‑extendible period of two months from mailing date of the notice of Final Refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal follows rules on appeal in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications accepted as complete are assigned to Examiners by class and shall be taken up for examination in the order filed. Amended applications are taken up in order of the date of response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and Completeness of Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application, the Examiner shall make a thorough study and investigation of available prior art; examination shall be complete with respect to compliance with statutes/rules and patentability and matters of form unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant will be notified of Examiner's action with reasons for adverse action and references useful to judge propriety of continuing prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of Examiner's Action and Standard Action Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner's action shall be comprehensive and complete in raising substantive matters, though may limit to restriction or fundamental defects first. Matters of form need not be raised until claims are found allowable. A standard action form shall be used containing merits, pertinent prior art and other matters affecting patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of Claims — Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: If invention not patentable in any manner all claims will be refused. If some claims are patentable and others not, only the latter will be refused and patent may still be granted for allowable claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In refusals for want of novelty or inventive step, Examiner must cite the most relevant references, designate the particular part relied on where necessary and clearly explain pertinence. Claims may be refused for non‑compliance with Sections 35.1 and 36.1 of the IP Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished Applications Not Citable as Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpublished pending applications and unpublished withdrawn/forfeited applications shall not be cited as prior art references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Reply Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: After an adverse Examiner action, applicant may reply and request re‑examination/reconsideration with or without amendment. To be entitled to re‑examination the applicant must request in writing and distinctly and specifically point out alleged Examiner errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must respond to every ground of objection/refusal (except form matters requested to be held in abeyance) and the response must appear bona fide to advance the case. Mere allegation of Examiner error insufficient. When amending in response to refusal, applicant must clearly point out novel and inventive features and show how amendments avoid cited references or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination and Reconsideration after Applicant Response
rubrics_metrics.description: After applicant response the application will be re‑examined and reconsidered; applicant will be notified if claims still refused or objections made. Amendments introduced after the second Examiner action shall relate only to matters that are subject of the refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Refusal or Action — Limitations and Reiteration
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination the refusal or objection may be declared final. Applicant's recourse is limited to filing an appeal or petition. In making final refusal, Examiner shall reiterate all grounds of refusal previously considered and may not cite additional grounds not previously raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition for final objections not involving claim refusal; Appeal for final refusal involving claims not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to Utility Model Application
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time before grant or refusal of a patent, applicant may convert to a utility model registration upon payment of fee; conversion allowed only once and the utility model is accorded filing date of initial application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition Against Parallel Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may not file two applications for same subject — one for utility model and one for patent, simultaneously or consecutively. If multiple applications cover the same subject matter, only the one with prior filing or priority date shall be considered; others deemed forfeited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments by the Applicant — No New Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may amend during examination provided such amendment does not include new matter outside scope of the disclosure contained in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final action may be introduced during appeal for deleting claims, complying with form, or presenting refused claims in better form. Amendments after final refusal may be admitted upon showing good cause and sufficient justification why not earlier presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and Revision Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Description, claims and drawings must be amended and revised when required to correct inaccuracies, remove unnecessary prolixity, and secure correspondence between description, claims, and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Broadening of Disclosure After Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: No deletion or addition shall broaden the disclosure of an application to include new matter after the filing date. All post‑filing amendments must conform to at least one version as of the filing date; matter not found in the original disclosure cannot be added even with supplemental oath and can only be claimed in a separate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Claims — Basis and Avoidance of References
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be amended by canceling claims, presenting new claims, or amending language. When presenting new or amended claims applicant must point out how they avoid any reference or ground of refusal and indicate which part of the original disclosure constitutes the basis for the amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of Making Amendments — Formal Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Erasures, additions, insertions, or alterations of papers and records must not be made by the applicant. Amendments are made by filing a request for amendment together with a clean copy of the amended text; exact words to be stricken or inserted and the precise point must be specified and basis in original application indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and Consideration of Amendments by the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are entered by the Office by drawing a line in red ink through words cancelled and making substitutions/insertions in red ink or by reference for large insertions. Ordinarily all amendments filed while application is open to amendments are entered and considered; untimely amendatory papers may be refused entry or considered in whole or in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Drawings — Permission and Formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: No change in the drawing may be made except by permission of the Office. Request for changes must include a sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes and be filed separately; drawing may not be pulled out except for signature and substitute drawings not ordinarily admitted unless required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Amendments — Rewriting Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendatory clause is to be amended it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion cancelled so no interlineations/deletions appear in the clause as finally presented. Matters cancelled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the cancelled matter as a new insertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute Description Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number or nature of amendments renders it difficult to consider the case or arrange papers for printing/copying, Examiner may require the entire description, claims or any part to be rewritten. A substitute description not ordinarily accepted unless required and may be required within two months from grant prior to publication.
